name: Anna Hazare
role: Indian Gandhian social activist; leader of the Ralegan Siddhi village model and of the 2011 Jan Lokpal anti-corruption movement
summary: Gandhian rural reformer and anti-corruption campaigner who ran a village development programme in Ralegan Siddhi with bans on alcohol, tobacco and tree felling and who led hunger strikes for the Right to Information, a Lokpal ombudsman, the right to recall and reject, and farmers' consent to land acquisition. He rejects political parties and electoral politics, insists on non-violence while backing the death penalty for corruption, and has said he would fight Pakistan over Kashmir.

recall-officials.rationale: He campaigns for a Right to Recall elected representatives, calling it a necessary part of the systemic change needed to curb corruption.

recallable-delegates.rationale: He demands a right to recall elected representatives as part of the combination of measures against corruption, though he does not discuss recall 'at any time' as such.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: He says politicians are not concerned about society or the State and are interested only in power and money.

one-party-rule.rationale: He argues that parties destroyed democracy, that the Constitution does not mention a party system, and that voters should choose independent candidates.

decide-locally.rationale: He campaigned to give power back to the gram sabha, the village assembly, and ran Ralegan Siddhi on village-level decisions.

participatory-democracy.rationale: In Ralegan Siddhi villagers decided and built through the gram sabha and shramdaan under his leadership.

public-access-to-information.rationale: He says he fought for the Right to Information Act because people have the right to know how public money is spent.

consent-of-governed.rationale: He says elected members are the people's trustees, that people are the masters and no one is above them.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: He argues that no one but the President is immune from investigation and that the Lokpal should cover the Prime Minister.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Under his leadership Ralegan ended untouchability: the dalit households, once ostracised, were brought into village life and housing.

death-penalty.rationale: He is reported saying he has always held that anyone found guilty of corruption should be hanged.

political-violence-legitimate.rationale: He says all his agitations were non-violent, that he never used the language of violence and that his movement will stay non-violent even facing lathis.

civil-disobedience-accept-penalty.rationale: He urged supporters to fill the jails, calling jail a matter of pride for a just cause, and said he would go to jail if stopped from fasting.

state-harmful.rationale: He campaigns for state institutions (a Lokpal, CBI under it, hanging for corruption) and says he believes in the Constitution.

dynastic-succession.rationale: He names nepotism as the biggest hindrance to development and the source of fraud and bribery.

simple-living.rationale: He lives in a small temple room without property or family, and says people keep increasing their needs and that this drives corruption.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: He says the race to acquire things puzzles him and that rising needs drive corruption.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: He writes that his army colleagues attained martyrdom in 1965 and honours Bhagat Singh and Rajguru as having laid down their lives for freedom.

sacred-nation.rationale: He says the nation is a temple and that serving the nation and its people is serving God.

limit-population.rationale: Ralegan Siddhi under his leadership adopted nasbandi (sterilisation) as one of four village bans, as part of the value system he set.

human-caused-global-warming.rationale: He says exploiting petrol, diesel, coal and natural resources causes pollution and rising temperatures, melting glaciers.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: He says development based on petrol, diesel and coal causes pollution and diseases, and his village works on energy that does not exploit nature.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: He served fifteen years in the army and says he is ready to take part in war against Pakistan again.

farm-price-support.rationale: Demanded in letters and threatened hunger strikes that the Centre implement the Swaminathan Commission's farm-price recommendations and give the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices autonomy; he fasted in support of the 2020 Bharat Bandh against the farm laws.
